note: Small, quiet family-run resort (since 1928) on the shore of Lax Lake in the Sawtooth hills inland from Silver Bay. No pets except certified medical dogs. Cell service is poor. --Claude
summary: Operator site read: 15 campsites, only two taking a motorhome/pull-through (to 32 ft), 20/30-amp electric, no water/sewer; lodge bathrooms, coin showers, laundry, store; mid-June to fall colours; phone/mail bookings only. Fees added ($48 two adults + $6 electric; page last updated for 2024). Google 4.7 (86). Not waterfront kept.
flags: PRICE GATE (private, no gateway within 40 km: gateways.py 'none within 40 km; nearest Isle Royale NP 140 km'): base $48 a night for two adults on a site without electric; with electric $54 ($48 + $6); a one-night weekend stay adds $5 ($53 / $59); credit cards add 3.99%. Whether either of the two motorhome sites can be had without electric is not stated ('Electric hookups are available for most sites'). Borderline: $48 passes, the realistic electric night at $54 is over $50. Rates are undated; the contact page still says 'Now taking reservations for 2024!', so the newest date on the site is 2024. Not a Good Sam Park (no claim found). Google Maps 4.7 from 86 reviews (strong) - per AWH 2026-10-30 a borderline price is decided on reviews.

Presence: passes (working operator site with phone 218-353-7424; Google Maps open, 4.7/86, same phone and website). RoverPass listing 'isBookable: false' (unclaimed, request only) - not cited. No booking engine: phone or mail with a one-night deposit.

Fit: only TWO of 15 sites take a motorhome ('Two sites can accomodate a pull-thru camper or motorhome... up to 32\''); a 23-ft rig fits those two. The rest are for tents, pop-ups, toppers and hammocks.
Long-stay tests: not long-stay in character (nightly rates per family unit, seasonal mid-June to fall, no monthly/seasonal sites marketed). Pass.

Waterfront: keep not waterfront (could not place the two motorhome sites). On imagery the resort's cabins and lodge stand 30-45 m from the Lax Lake shore on the lake side of Lax Lake Road, under trees; the camp sites are not visible and the site does not say where the two pull-throughs are. Lead only: the page's tone ('wouldn't you rather listen to the soft lapping of waves') suggests lakeside sites, but nothing places an RV site on open ground within 50 m.
Phone 218-353-7424 and website https://www.laxlakeresort.com/ confirmed (operator site and Google).
Policy: no pets ('NO PET POLICY (with the exception of certified medical dogs)'); day visitors pay a $5 visitor pass; one vehicle and one family unit per site.
